anomalies.observed: The MCU PWM pins U2.6/U3.6, the PMOS gate Q1.1, the NPN collector Q2.3, and one side of the base resistor R2.1 are all on net PWM; R2.2 is on Net-(Q2-B), so R2 connects the collector/gate node back to the NPN base.
anomalies.expected: For the high-side PMOS switch, the MCU output should drive Q2's base through R2 (MCU -> R2 -> Q2.B), while Q2.C should be the PWM/gate node pulled up by R1; the MCU pin should not be tied to the collector/gate node with R2 forming base-collector feedback.
anomalies.impact: The PWM node cannot be driven high: when it rises above about 0.7 V Q2 conducts and pulls it down, keeping Q1 on and preventing normal fan PWM/power control; it may also cause excessive MCU pin current/contention.

parsed.summary: The connectivity around Q2/R2 is anomalous: the MCU and PMOS gate are tied to the NPN collector, and R2 feeds that same node back to the base, creating a clamp/feedback path instead of a base-drive level shifter.
